subject: Client disconnect storm: streaming sessions dropping and 429 surge
messages:
From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@neurolink.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@neurolink.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden increase in client-side timeouts / streaming drops

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in streaming disconnects and 429s yesterday afternoon. Our telemetry shows ~18% of active chat sessions for power users are dropping mid-completion between 10–30s, and our SDK reports a sequence of rapid reconnect attempts (~3 retries with no exponential backoff) that appear to correlate with the spike of 429 responses.

This is affecting the new conversational triage flow we launched last week — customers are reporting hallucinated partial results and then blank responses after retries. Impact: high — two pilot customers temporarily turned off the feature.

I've attached a small dump of recent client logs and a short timeline. Can Redwood confirm whether this is something on your side (throttling, autoscaler oscillation) or if our SDK is misbehaving? We need a short-lived mitigation we can push to clients while you diagnose.

Thanks,
Sara Mitchell
Head of Product, NeuroLink Health

Subject: Fwd: sudden increase in client-side timeouts / streaming drops

Rishi — forwarding NeuroLink's logs and timeline (attached).

Prelim notes from our side:
- We see a short-lived burst of 429s originating from the hosted inference pool that serves their region between 15:04–15:22 UTC.
- Autoscaler shows oscillation: a small surge > scale-up > then scale-down within ~2m which likely left some requests rejected.
- Client logs show immediate retry attempts without jitter/backoff which amplifies the 429s into a retry storm.

Suggested immediate mitigations:
1) Recommend NeuroLink apply client-side maximum-backoff + jitter (we can provide a snippet).
2) Temporarily raise their concurrency limit / burst capacity for the next 6 hours (we should gate by account).
3) Enable streaming keepalive probe to reduce idle disconnects while we debug.

Attaching: nl_chat_dumps_0304.tar.gz and the 429 spike graph.

-Ben
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden increase in client-side timeouts / streaming drops

Thanks Ben — we've dug into the infra traces. Short summary:
- Root cause appears to be an interaction between our autoscaler aggressive scale-in policy and a bursty traffic pattern from a small set of long-lived streaming sessions.
- When a node scales down it forces some in-flight streaming connections to be drained; those clients rapidly reconnect and our rate limiter returns 429s. The clients' retry behavior lacks exponential backoff, which leads to retry amplification.

Immediate plan (T+0 to T+4 hours):
- T+0: Apply a targeted temporary concurrency bump for NeuroLink's tenant (increase reserved capacity on the pool).
- T+0: Flip the keepalive/idle-timeout extension for streaming (increase idle window from 30s -> 120s) for affected pool to avoid premature disconnects.
- T+0: Publish a recommended backoff snippet to NeuroLink (we'll include jitter + cap).
- T+2h: Monitor 429/5xx at the pool level and client-side reconnect rates.
- T+4h: If stable, roll a conservative autoscaler scale-in cooldown to reduce oscillation.

Related artifacts: runbook_stream_restart.md (attached), link to RF-4521 for postmortem.

I'll kick off a short war room and post the dial-in. Laura — tagging for visibility because NeuroLink is an impacted pilot and this may need exec-level comms (credits / SLA exceptions).

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

- Increased reserved concurrency for NeuroLink's tenant and enabled an expanded streaming idle timeout for the affected pool.
- Published a short client-side backoff + jitter snippet for your SDK (attached).
- We will monitor closely and have a war room scheduled now (invite sent).

Customer-facing language (you can paste this):
"\nWe're aware of intermittent chat completions timing out and some clients observing blank responses after quick reconnects. Our engineers implemented an immediate mitigation: increased dedicated capacity for your tenant and extended stream idle timeouts, and we've delivered a client-side backoff snippet to prevent retry amplification. We will continue monitoring and will provide an RCA within 5 business days.\n"

Next steps:
- War room now — dial-in in the calendar invite.
- We'll follow up with a short timeline for the RCA and proposed long-term autoscaler tuning.

Thanks for flagging this, and apologies for the disruption. We'll keep you updated.
